factory_reusable: Production handoff records, outage drill records, runbook replay evidence, rollback paths, observability, incident paths, support paths, and operator signoff must be machine-checked.

node_contract.when: Before future release handoffs or operator readiness records are trusted.
node_contract.who: Codex as responsible fixer; human owner as Ralph-loop driver and accountable production approver.
node_contract.how_good: Templates, unsigned drills, missing rollback paths, and low readiness reject while complete pass fixtures accept.

expert_debate.system_theorist: A factory that hands production to humans without executable readiness evidence is incomplete at the final control boundary.
expert_debate.requirements_governance_architect: The handoff must bind release ownership, rollback, observability, incident path, support path, runbook replay, and signoff to the same ledger and gate model as other artifacts.
expert_debate.verification_safety_critic: Templates and low-readiness drills must fail automatically; otherwise the proof is decorative.
expert_debate.synthesis: Install a focused validator and add positive and negative fixtures to the regular hardening runner.

human_decisions: Human owner requested pass 26 and asked to fix any new findings.
assumptions: Pass 26 is a patch-level production/SRE handoff hardening pass, not a full production game-day simulation.
risks: Validator proves structure and linkage, not real operator performance in a live system.
A full production simulation and runtime dashboard remain future work.
